payload: architecture/overview/index.yaml plus recursive architecture/sds/**/index.yaml leaves carrying source-independent specification@3; branches aggregate.
sourceTruth: Canonical Work intent and design constraints, not code.
completion: Current design review in Work, never source implementation or executed recovery. Existing legacy completion transport remains readable, not fabricated.
handoff: Reference canonical SRS and SDS IDs without copying. Implementation owns repository/file/symbol/commit mapping and actual tests.

action.en: Resolve current accepted SRS scope, drivers, actors and platform constraints from canonical .starciwork. Read specifications/sds.schema.json, docs/architecture-sds.md and docs/source-of-trust.md. Begin every new or revised SDS with complete journey and responsibility analysis, not a legacy call graph. Architecture is source-independent: no source paths, symbols, revisions, codeImpacts, repository audit or test-command inventory. Code and green tests do not authorize the target design; a design constraint does not prove deployed behavior.

Write logical components with responsibilities, exclusions and dependency directions. Contracts have one owner, caller/receiver, sync/async/in-process mode, inputs, outcomes/errors, authority, timeout, retry, idempotency and compatibility. Import shared views by stable Work/view IDs; never copy or redefine another owner contract.

Design runtime scenarios referencing canonical SRS flow IDs. Every step names its component, contracts, data, commit point, failure outcome and recovery. Cover significant architectural differences, including response loss, concurrency, duplicates, ordering, partial success and cancellation where relevant.

Specify authoritative versus rebuildable data, storage, isolation, consistency, lifecycle, placement, connections and credential custody. For durable customer state, specify the selected backup/restore form, capture consistency, complete retained stores/objects/runtime state/config/Secrets/keys, independent custody, destination, compatibility, restore order, verification and safe resumption. A generic supports-restore promise, recreated configuration or module reinstall does not explain data recovery. Select failure domains and HA/recovery depth from actual scope, not a mandatory cluster-loss checklist for every project.

Challenge one coherent proposal with a materially simpler alternative, rationale, cost, downsides and revisit conditions. Patterns are optional; specify actual mechanisms rather than names. Use applicable knowledge and primary technical references with an applicability argument. Do not invent business targets or product policy; make technical choices within approved requirements.

Write relevant quality/threat/failure scenarios with trigger, impact, response, owner and planned design checks linked to SRS acceptance. Keep residual risk and limitations explicit. Never claim source implementation, security audit, HA verification or a recovery drill ran from a design document.

Validate recursive layout and exact canonical SRS/shared-design references, then walk complete significant journeys as an implementer: each component, connection, state owner, success/partial/uncertain outcome and next permitted action must be unambiguous. Review full requirement/flow/acceptance coverage, shared consumer consistency and simpler alternatives across the owning scope. Resolve known material design blockers before pass and record concrete findings and resolutions; this does not require perfect foresight of all future cases. Gaps found during review, coding, testing, operation or later customer feedback require scoped SRS/SDS repair within authority and current reviewed done before dependent effects. Do not reopen unrelated design or rewrite requirements to justify legacy code. Schema validity alone is not review. Implementation owns source mapping and test execution; done is never an edit lock.
